subject: Audit logs — residency, export formats, and deletion playbook
messages:

Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on audit log export & deletion proof for EU tenant

Hi Vanessa,

Quick follow-up from our compliance team after the demo — they want a clear bullet list of what Redwood can provide for our EU tenant regarding audit/access logs. Specifically: 

- Retention windows you support for audit logs (by default and for paid retention add-ons)
- Export formats available (CSV, JSON, compressed bundles) and whether exported events include full request/response metadata or just action traces
- Whether exports can be scoped by org, tenant, or user ID and filtered by time ranges
- Proof-of-deletion workflow: if we request erasure of a tenant, how do you demonstrate logs have been removed from active and cold storage (and timing)
- Support for signed handover (S3 with server-side encryption + signed manifest) and whether Redwood will provide an attestation letter

Can you give us a playbook and an estimated lead time for a standard export + deletion attestation? We’d like this for our legal/infosec review.

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear checklist. I’m looping in Ben (account lead) to coordinate timelines and Karthik (security) for the technical playbook. High-level answers below; we’ll attach a one-page playbook and field mapping for your review.

- Retention windows: default hosted audit retention is 90 days. We offer add-ons up to 7 years via our Evidence Retention Add-on (contracted). For Dedicated/Private we can configure per-customer retention policies.

- Export formats: full exports supported as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and CSV bundles. Exports include event timestamp, actor (user/service principal), action, resource, request_id, and contextual metadata (IP, region, model id). Full request/response payloads are not included by default for privacy — can be added under a scoped data-access agreement.

- Scoping: exports can be filtered by tenant_id, org_id, user_id, and arbitrary time ranges. We can also provide pre-sliced exports (e.g., monthly chunks) for large windows.

- Proof-of-deletion: we provide a three-stage workflow — mark-for-deletion (0–72h), purge from hot stores (up to 7 days depending on shard), and tombstone/erase from cold indexes (30–90 days depending on archive cycle). For EU tenants we provide an attestation manifest and SHA256 checksums of deleted archive bundles.

- Signed handover: we support direct S3 pushes to your bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). We provide a signed manifest and optional human-signed attestation PDF.

Attached: audit-export-playbook.pdf (playbook + estimated timeline), export-field-mapping.csv.

Ben, Karthik — can you confirm the technical steps and an expected calendar for a standard one-month export + deletion attestation (non-legal hold)? Elena — happy to schedule a quick call if helpful.

Best,

On Sat, 02 May 2026 at 10:05, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com wrote:
> Attached: audit-export-playbook.pdf (playbook + estimated timeline), export-field-mapping.csv.

Elena — below is a concise technical playbook and estimated SLA for a standard export + deletion attestation for an EU tenant (non-legal-hold). I’ll keep it prescriptive so your engineers can map it to internal processes.

1) Scope & Request intake (Day 0)
- Customer submits export request form + S3 destination details and IAM role (if using customer S3). For Redwood-hosted transfer, provide pre-signed upload link.
- We validate tenant_id, time-range, and scope filters.

2) Export preparation (Day 1–2)
- Generate a dry-run estimate of data volume and slice into 24/72h batches as requested.
- Produce field-mapping CSV (attached) and sample 1-hour bundle for verification.

3) Export execution (Day 3–5, depends on volume)
- Stream events into ndjson files and compress with gzip. Files are signed (SHA256) and uploaded to target S3.
- For large exports we use parallelized workers and provide a transfer manifest with checksums and byte counts.

4) Verification & Attestation (Day 5–7)
- Customer verifies sample bundles; Redwood issues a signed manifest (PDF) and optional human-signed attestation stating the scope and time window.

5) Deletion playbook (if deletion requested after handover)
- Mark-for-deletion: set retention flag (t=0). Records are excluded from live queries immediately.
- Hot-store purge: background job purges hot shards (up to 7 days depending on sequence windows).
- Cold-store tombstone & archive erase: triggered on next archive cycle; outcome typically within 30–90 days.
- Post-deletion attestation: we provide an erase manifest listing bundle names, deletion timestamps, and SHA256 of the removed archives.

Notes / Constraints
- Legal holds: if there is a legal hold on the tenant or specific users, deletion is postponed until the hold is released.
- Immutable backups: snapshots in immutable backup systems are retained per contract; we can provide explicit retention/erase terms in the SOW.
- Requesting full request/response payloads increases compliance review and often requires a custom Data Processing Addendum.

Estimated timelines: standard 1-month export + deletion attestation = 7–30 business days depending on data volume and contracted priorities. Expedited handling available under an express SOW.

If this maps to BrightLine’s expectations I can draft the technical appendix text for your DPA and SOW.

-Karthik
